inputs.original_text: Folks, let’s be entirely clear about what is happening here: we are witnessing disaster capitalism in real time, driven by unregulated global capitalism and predatory external forces. Decades of systemic inequality and institutional impoverishment have left ordinary Cuban residents owning nothing and struggling in poverty, structurally barred from taking over the few functioning businesses on the island. And who is waiting in the wings to capitalize on this manufactured vulnerability? A wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the exact playbook of disaster capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.
inputs.modified_text: Let’s call this what it is: classic, predatory disaster capitalism making its move. Decades of systemic inequality and institutional impoverishment have been weaponized against ordinary Cuban residents, leaving them owning nothing, struggling in poverty, and structurally barred from taking over the few functioning businesses on the island. And right on cue, a wealthy diaspora community and foreign investors are circling, ready to swoop in and buy property and businesses at bargain prices. This is the exact playbook of global capitalism—stripping the assets of working people and handing community wealth over to the privileged few, while completely bypassing any collective ownership or labor rights for the people who actually built and sustained that society.
